body:
AI voice agent pricing depends on three line items: the platform that runs the agent, the large language model (LLM) that powers each conversation, and the telephony provider that connects your calls. Most pricing pages lead with a monthly plan fee, but that fee covers only the first of those three.

This guide explains how AI voice agent pricing works, what sets your price per minute, and how to calculate ROI against your current staffing costs.

We use real ElevenAgents pricing throughout, so you have concrete figures to plan with.

## Summary

• Your voice agent cost equals platform minutes plus LLM usage plus telephony, and the LLM and telephony costs are billed separately at cost.

• ElevenAgents plans run from a free tier with 15 minutes per month to custom Enterprise pricing. Every paid tier works out to $0.08 per platform minute.

• A plan's concurrent call limit determines how many calls your agent handles at once, which matters as much as the per-minute rate.

• The free tier and the Startup Grants Program cover prototyping and early builds, but production volume carries real LLM and telephony costs.

• Compare total agent cost against the fully loaded cost of human staffing for the same call volume, adjusted for the share of calls the agent resolves end to end.

## AI voice agent pricing at a glance

ElevenAgents uses tiered monthly plans. Each tier includes a set number of call minutes, a concurrent call limit, and features that scale with team size.

Divide any paid plan's price by its included minutes, and you get the same platform rate: $0.08 per minute. Additional minutes on Creator and above bill at that same $0.08 rate, and text messages cost $0.003 each. Prices exclude taxes. Because every paid tier shares the same platform rate, volume discounts come through custom Enterprise pricing.

The table shows platform cost only. LLM usage and telephony sit on top, which the next two sections explain.

## How AI voice agent pricing models work

The providers of AI voice agents tend to price their offerings in one of three main ways, with many often blending more than one. These models include:

• Usage-based pricing: You pay per minute or per call. Costs track volume directly, which suits teams with variable or seasonal traffic.

• Seat-based pricing: You pay per user who builds, manages, or monitors agents. This model appears most often on business and enterprise tiers.

• Flat subscription tiers: You pay a fixed monthly fee that includes a minute allowance. This gives predictable budgeting up to the allowance.

ElevenAgents combines all three. Each plan has a fixed monthly fee with included minutes, per-minute billing for additional usage, and workspace seats on the Scale and Business tiers.

When you compare AI voice agent pricing models, check one detail first: whether the advertised per-minute rate is all-in or platform-only. A platform-only rate with LLM and telephony billed at cost gives you visibility into each line item. A bundled rate hides the split, which makes it harder to optimize.

## What determines your AI voice agent price per minute?

Your effective price per minute is the sum of three separate line items. Treat them as distinct budgets, because each one responds to different decisions.

Total monthly cost = (call minutes × platform rate) + LLM usage + telephony

## Platform cost

The platform rate covers the voice and conversation layer. On ElevenAgents, that includes text to speech , speech to text , turn taking , knowledge bases, and RAG .

Voice quality sits inside this rate. Eleven v4 Turbo in ElevenAgents runs at a median inference latency of about 100 ms across more than 90 languages.

## LLM cost

The LLM reasons through each turn of the conversation, and its cost varies by model. ElevenAgents bills LLM usage at cost , so a larger reasoning model costs more per minute than a lighter one.

Match the model to the task. Routine requests such as order status or appointment changes rarely need the most capable model, while complex troubleshooting often does.

## Telephony cost

Telephony connects your agent to the phone network. Carriers bill at their own rates, and ElevenAgents passes those through at cost.

Your telephony spend depends on your provider, number type, and call direction. Web and in-app voice conversations through the widget skip carrier charges entirely.

## Concurrency and burst capacity

Concurrency is the number of calls your agent handles at the same moment. A plan with 20 concurrent calls supports 20 simultaneous conversations, no matter how many minutes remain in your allowance.

Size your plan against peak hour traffic, not monthly totals. ElevenAgents also lists a burst rate of $0.16 per minute for call spikes beyond standard capacity, and Enterprise plans offer elevated concurrency limits.

## Average AI voice agent pricing by use case

No single average exists, because the range from $0 to custom Enterprise pricing reflects different use cases rather than inconsistent pricing. A useful way to estimate is to translate plan minutes into calls.

Assuming a four-minute average call, here is how the tiers map to real workloads:

• Prototyping and testing: The Free ($0) and Starter ($6 per month) plans cover early builds and internal demos, with 15 and 75 minutes per month.

• Small business support: The Pro plan ($99 per month) includes 1,238 minutes, covering roughly 300 calls per month, enough for a single location handling inbound questions.

• Growing support teams: The Scale plan ($299 per month) includes 3,738 minutes, covering about 930 calls per month, with three workspace seats for the team managing the agent.
